title: e2e examples registry
description: Every example listed on https://e2e.tester.army/examples: the official ones (folders under examples/ and repositories in the tester-army organization), partners' and the community's own repositories. `node scripts/check-examples.ts` validates the file against this schema and checks what a schema cannot: unique slugs, known tags, and existing icons and folders.

tags.description: The tags an example can carry, one list per kind. Each kind is a filter on the site, its tags the filter's options in this order.

framework.description: The stack the example's app is built with.

useCase.description: What the example shows, beyond its stack: a starter app, authentication, visual testing.

slug.description: The page's address, unique across the registry: https://e2e.tester.army/examples/<slug>. `opengraph-image` is taken by the site's own route.

shortTitle.description: The name on the example's card, when shorter than the title: "Vite".

description.description: One or two sentences on the card and under the page's heading.

icon.description: The example's logo, a file in examples/icons/ (SVG or PNG). Without one the site shows the e2e logo, the default for every example that is not about one framework or one company's product.

invertIcon.description: For a logo drawn in black for light backgrounds: the site shows it inverted, in white.

source.description: `official` for the examples the e2e team maintains, in the tester-army organization; `partner` for the ones a partner company verifies and maintains in its own repository, outside it, shown with a partner seal on the site; `community` for everyone else's, outside it.

repository.description: The example's folder on GitHub, whose README the page renders: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>, or https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/tree/<ref>/<path> for a folder.

github.description: The GitHub user or organization: the avatar and the profile link.

website.description: A partner's landing page, linked from the partner's name on the site. Required on a partner example, and only there.

licenseUrl.description: Where the license text lives. Without it the site links to the license on spdx.org.

framework.description: Tag ids from tags.framework, the main one first.
